method: each falsifying hypothesis for the current proposal (C) checked against gathered evidence; verdicts SUPPORTED / PARTIAL / REJECTED / UNTESTED

findings.hypothesis: minimal Mutation IR cannot represent normal control behavior without awkward expansion
findings.evidence: 17 straight-line + 73 loop-fill scripts (~78%) fit a minimal IR with a fill primitive; 25/115 (styles, xml/zip, struct ops, conditional targets) do not; awkward-expansion cases (conditional targets, programmatic program choice) unmeasured
findings.implication: a minimal IR is lossy; B/C must either grow the IR (complexity) or concede ~22% of mutations (two-tier system)

findings.hypothesis: forcing structured mutations removes useful Python flexibility
findings.evidence: 0 calc_translate_fill invocations despite explanation; agents considered then chose openpyxl (4 tasks); 5/13 calc_query adoption; census shows flexibility actually used (charts, zip repair, conditional logic)
findings.implication: adoption resistance is measured, not hypothetical; forced-IR capability test is mandatory before B/C

findings.hypothesis: compiled query tools merely duplicate cheap Python operations
findings.evidence: for: Spark O7 solved from raw facts; forced-05_01 identical miss; QUERIED_BUT_WRONG_MODEL_CHOICE. against: 474 scan-loops + 527 re-opens show Python ops are cheap-per-call but numerous; latency comparison UNTESTED
findings.implication: duplication claim undecided; efficiency replay needed, capability claim rejected

findings.hypothesis: runtime interception would be too incomplete to trust
findings.evidence: no capture prototype exists; but corpus for a byte-identity completeness proof exists (707 scripts, 115 mutating)
findings.implication: D's risk is concrete and cheaply testable zero-model; do not assert infeasibility

findings.hypothesis: deterministic components save negligible model work
findings.evidence: mutation-side: Phase C halved sessions/tokens in old arch; inspection-side (the larger center) untouched by any deterministic component so far; compact encoding saved only 14.5% and added timeouts
findings.implication: savings are real but concentrated; inspection cost is the unaddressed center

findings.hypothesis: most control cost is semantic reasoning rather than mechanics
findings.evidence: T2 (9/14 FCVW) semantic upstream failures; NOVEL_SYNTHESIS_DOMINANT; construction failures with operands in hand (6/11); but ~1M prompt tokens/task with 474 scan loops suggests large mechanical share; no decomposition measured
findings.implication: both matter; the audit cannot apportion — a trajectory work-center decomposition is owed (Phase 9 partially delivered via ledgers + census)

findings.hypothesis: compiled substrate maintenance costs more than it saves
findings.evidence: no maintenance-cost accounting exists; failure mode observed instead: stale/empty artifacts (prep temporal placeholders, scalar-omitting caches) silently served wrong evidence — staleness is the demonstrated risk, cost is not
findings.implication: substrate needs freshness invariants (rebuild-on-placeholder, scalar completeness gate) before cost debate

findings.hypothesis: old positive mechanisms only repair old-architecture-induced failures
findings.evidence: 4/5 induced-failure cases classify ARCHITECTURE_INDUCED; translation and closure wins do not reproduce under default agent (08_03 no-headroom; T3=0); residue that is natural: one-shot program choice, upstream semantic correctness, inspection cost
findings.implication: the strongest falsifier: carry mechanisms forward ONLY in narrow roles tied to default-agent cost centers, never as restoration of old coordination
